# Installing Packages

# Introduction

This report will examine the locations of Airbnb properties within Austin, Texas and their relation to other socio-economic demographics within the city. This is significantly relevant research as their is growing discourse around the negative impact of holiday rentals on minority/vulnerable residents in urban areas.

# Body

The analysis uses listings and neighborhood datasets from the Airbnb website as well as US census data for the different social demographics. The listings data

```{r Austin Population Race}
austin_race <- get_acs(
  state = "TX",

  output = "wide",
  year = 2022
)

austin_race <- austin_race %>%
  select(-NAME) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
```

## Join

```{r}
# join_all(list(la_race, XXXXXadd_in_all_your_other_dataframes)
austin_all <- join_all(list(austin_race), by='GEOID', type='left')

st_write(austin_all, "ACS_austin_2018_2022_vars.csv", append=FALSE)

austin_plot <- st_as_sf(left_join(austin, 
                       austin_all, 
                       by='GEOID'), wkt = "geometry", crs = 32139)
```

```{r}
austin_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(fill = black)) + 
  geom_sf(color = NA) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") 
```

```{r}
austin_hisp <- get_acs(
  state = "TX",
  county = c(austin = "Travis County"),
  geography = "tract",
  table = "B03003",
  output = "wide",
  year = 2022
) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    total_pop = B03003_001E,
    hispanic = B03003_003E
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_hispanic = hispanic / total_pop * 100
  )
```

```{r}
austin_density <- austin %>%
  st_transform(NAD83) %>%                     # project for accurate area
  mutate(
    area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, area_km2)
```

```{r}
austin_density <- left_join(austin_hisp %>% select(GEOID, total_pop),
                            austin_density,
                            by="GEOID") %>%
  mutate(pop_density = total_pop / area_km2)
```

```{r}
austin_unemp <- get_acs(
  state = "TX",
  county = c(austin = "Travis County"),
  geography = "tract",
  table = "DP03",
  output = "wide",
  year = 2022
)

austin_unemp <- austin_unemp %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    labor_force = DP03_0002E,
    unemployed  = DP03_0005E
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    unemp_rate = unemployed / labor_force * 100
  )
```

```{r}
austin_age <- get_acs(
  state = "TX",
  county = c(austin = "Travis County"),
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B01002_001",   # median age
  year = 2022
) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, median_age = estimate)
```

```{r}
austin_race      <- st_drop_geometry(austin_race)
austin_income    <- st_drop_geometry(austin_income)
austin_hisp      <- st_drop_geometry(austin_hisp)
austin_density   <- st_drop_geometry(austin_density)
austin_unemp     <- st_drop_geometry(austin_unemp)
austin_age       <- st_drop_geometry(austin_age)

#names(austin_unemp)

austin_all <- join_all(
  list(
    austin_race,
    austin_income,
    austin_hisp,
    austin_density,
    austin_unemp,
    austin_age
  ),
  by = "GEOID",
  type = "left"
)

names(austin_all)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries (if not already loaded)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tmap)

# 1. Perform the spatial join to count the points in each polygon
# This function finds which polygon each listing point is in, then groups and counts.

# First, ensure both austin_plot and listings_sf have the same CRS.
# Assuming they do, proceed with the join:

austin_with_counts <- st_join(austin_plot, listings_sf, join = st_intersects) %>%
  group_by(NAME_OF_AREA_COLUMN_IN_AUSTIN_PLOT) %>% # Replace this with the unique ID or name column of your areas
  summarise(listing_count = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

# NOTE: The exact column name for grouping (like 'NAME_OF_AREA_COLUMN_IN_AUSTIN_PLOT') 
# depends on the structure of your 'austin_plot' data frame. 
# Use the column that uniquely identifies each polygon (e.g., 'neighborhood', 'census_tract_id', etc.).
# 'austin_with_counts' is now an sf object ready for choropleth mapping.
```

```{r}
# Example with median income
austin_clean <- austin_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(med_income))

# Spatial neighbors & weights
nb <- poly2nb(austin_clean, queen = TRUE)
listw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W")

# Local Moran's I
local_moran <- localmoran(austin_clean$med_income, listw)

austin_clean <- austin_clean %>%
  mutate(
    Ii = local_moran[, "Ii"],
    E.Ii = local_moran[, "E.Ii"],
    Z.Ii = local_moran[, "Z.Ii"],
    Pr.z = local_moran[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"],
    avg_income_std = scale(med_income)[,1],
    lagged_income = lag.listw(listw, avg_income_std),
    quadrant = case_when(
      avg_income_std > 0 & lagged_income > 0 ~ "High-High",
      avg_income_std < 0 & lagged_income < 0 ~ "Low-Low",
      avg_income_std > 0 & lagged_income < 0 ~ "High-Low",
      avg_income_std < 0 & lagged_income > 0 ~ "Low-High",
      TRUE ~ "Not Significant"
    )
  )

tm_shape(austin_clean) +
  tm_polygons(col = "quadrant",
              palette = c("red", "blue", "pink", "lightblue", "gray80"),
              title = "LISA Cluster") +
  tm_layout(title = "Map 4: Local Moran's I – Median Income",
            legend.outside = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "top")) +
  tm_scale_bar(position = c("left", "bottom"))

```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# Keep only variables for clustering
acs_vars <- austin_plot %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(med_income, pct_hispanic, pop_density, unemp_rate, median_age)

# Remove rows with any missing values
acs_vars_clean <- acs_vars %>% filter(complete.cases(.))

# Standardize variables
acs_scaled <- scale(acs_vars_clean)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
k <- 4  # number of clusters
km_res <- kmeans(acs_scaled, centers = k, nstart = 25)

# Add cluster labels back to sf object
austin_plot$cluster <- NA
austin_plot$cluster[complete.cases(acs_vars)] <- km_res$cluster
```

```{r}
library(tmap)

tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(austin_plot) +
  tm_polygons("cluster",
              palette = "viridis",      # color-blind friendly
              title = "Geodemographic Cluster") +
  tm_scale_bar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Austin Geodemographic Clusters",
            legend.outside = TRUE)
```
